dedupe_keys.name: forestry commission map browser and land information search england

description: The Forestry Commission map browser lets users view data layers published by the Forestry Commission, draw features, measure boundaries and print maps, and its Land Information Search runs a report over more than 100 spatial data layers for an area of land in England. The report lists land designations and features such as National Nature Reserves, protected sites, priority habitats and peat soils, current grant schemes and felling permissions, and markers such as the Low Risk to Woodland Creation dataset, so that planners can see constraints and opportunities for woodland creation and whom to consult. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): OGL-UK-3.0 (GOV.UK site-wide statement: all content available under OGL v3.0 except where otherwise stated). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the search covers England only, not all forestry-relevant layers are in the browser (users are told to check MAGIC as well), and the service has planned downtime. It supports green infrastructure planning, such as siting new woodland and flood-reducing planting, and land constraint screening for infrastructure corridors; related records are the OS MasterMap Greenspace layer and the Copernicus tree cover layer.
